question.problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $N?$

I. $N∨(¬M∨N)$

II. $N∧(¬M∨N)$

III. $(¬M∨N)∧N$
question.worked_solution:
The law that conjunction absorbs disjunction is stated as

$$
N∧(N∨¬M)≡N.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is *not* logically equivalent to $N.$ This statement cannot be simplified using the absorption laws.

- Statement II is logically equivalent to $N.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}N∧(¬M∨N) & ≡N∧(N∨¬M) \\  & ≡N.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is logically equivalent to $N.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(¬M∨N)∧N & ≡N∧(¬M∨N) \\  & ≡N∧(N∨¬M) \\  & ≡N.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
